The `hunks` property for a renamed file is not tested. A rename appears as `--- a/old.py` / `+++ b/new.py`, meaning `paths` would include both names but `hunks` would key only on `new.py` (the `+++` side, after stripping `b/`). A finding citing `old.py` (the deleted side of a rename) would pass the `paths` check but get no hunk entry, and `_outside_every_hunk` would return `False` (the `not spans` short-circuit), keeping any line. That behaviour may be correct — it is the same path as a deleted …[truncated]

`hunks` strips a leading `b/` prefix from the `+++` name but `paths` strips neither `a/` nor `b/` from either side. So for a normal file `src/real.py`, `paths` contains `src/real.py` (from `+++ b/src/real.py` after `len('+++ b/')` = 6 chars stripped) — wait, `paths` strips the full marker `'+++ b/'` (6 chars), so it does store `src/real.py`. The `_PATHS_NAMED = 3` truncation path ("and N more") is not exercised. The test at line 1548 drops two paths and checks both appear in the message. A case with four or more distinct unreachable paths would trigger the truncation branch (`more > 0`). No test asserts that the "and N more" text appears, so a regression there would be silent. Missing assertion: `assert 'and 1 more' in refusals[0].message` for a four-path case.
